clips.title: Django REST Framework Oversimplified
clips.why: Dennis Ivy creates a model, migrates it and writes a serializer for it, the first two parts of every DRF endpoint, in a few unhurried minutes.
look: The model is a class whose fields become columns, and the migration commands turn it into a table.
The serializer lists which model fields go into the JSON.
How the view returns the serializer's data as the response.
clips.after: fcp's cloud has the same two layers for every object: a model in rhinoCore/models and a serializer in rhinoCore/serializers.

clips.title: Viewsets & Routers in Django REST Framework
clips.why: BugBytes replaces separate views with one viewset, which is the step that makes the projects endpoint in the story so short.
look: Why a viewset groups list, retrieve, create, update and delete for one kind of object.
What the viewset needs from you: which rows (a queryset) and which serializer.
What the viewset replaces from the earlier, separate views.
clips.after: fcp's ProjectViewSetRhino is this pattern, built from smaller mixins so it offers only the actions fcp allows.

clips.title: Testing APIs with Django REST Framework
clips.why: The same channel tests one endpoint with DRF's test client: send a request inside the test, then check the status code and the JSON.
look: The test sends the request through the test client; no server is started.
It checks the status code, then the data in the response.
Where the test's data comes from before the request is sent.
clips.after: fcp's planned API tests check endpoints the same way, with pytest-django instead of Django's test classes.

practice.q: A POST /api/projects/ arrives. Put the parts in the order they handle it.
items: The router matches projects/ and POST to the viewset's create action
The viewset hands the JSON body to the serializer
The serializer checks every field and turns the body into Python values
The model saves the new row through the ORM
The serializer turns the saved object into JSON, and the viewset answers 201
practice.why: URL first, then the action, then validation at the serializer's door, then the database, and the serializer again on the way out.

practice.q: You need a new read-only field, created_by, in the projects API response. Which file decides whether clients can see it and whether they can send it?

options.text: The serializer: its fields list makes it visible, and read_only_fields keeps clients from writing it.
options.why: The serializer is the API's door in both directions. The model only says what the table can store.

options.text: The router, by registering a new URL for the field.
options.why: Routers map URLs to actions. Fields are not routes.

options.text: The migration, because it adds the column.
options.why: The migration changes the table. Whether the API shows the column is the serializer's choice.

practice.q: This test talks to the database. Let pytest-django allow it for every test in the file.
practice.hint: The marker name the RuntimeError tells you to use.
practice.why: Database access is opt-in. With the django_db marker, each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back at the end.

practice.q: You changed a model. Ask Django to write the migration for the projects app.
practice.hint: Not migrate, which only applies migrations that already exist.
practice.why: makemigrations compares the models with the last migration and writes the next file. fcp's CI runs makemigrations --check --dry-run to catch a forgotten one.

practice.q: In fcp, GET /api/v2/projects/ returns an empty list for a new workgroup. Which part of the viewset decides which rows come back?

options.text: get_serializer_class, because it chooses the fields.
options.why: The serializer shapes each row, but it does not decide which rows exist in the answer.

options.text: get_queryset, the query that filters the rows this request may see.
options.why: An empty list means the query found no rows for this user and workgroup, which is exactly what RH-1234's card needs.
basename only names the URL patterns, such as project-list.
